research_mode: official Building Safety Regulator and GOV.UK primary guidance only; high-rise accountable-person, risk-assessment, safety-management and resident-engagement methodology gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Risk-assessment purpose
verified_claims: Assessing how safety incidents can happen helps accountable persons understand risks, manage them and demonstrate all reasonable steps.
limitations: A risk assessment supports decisions but is not proof that an incident will occur.

sources.name: Risk-team knowledge
verified_claims: A risk-assessment team should include knowledge and experience of safety management systems, fire safety and structural safety.
limitations: The listed disciplines do not by themselves demonstrate that a particular team is competent.

sources.name: Specialist involvement proportionality
verified_claims: The assessment team does not always have to include consultants, though specialist knowledge may be needed depending on the building.
limitations: This guidance must not be used to exclude specialists where complexity requires them.

sources.name: Area-specific hazards
verified_claims: Assessments should distinguish hazards in flats from hazards in halls, community rooms, plant rooms and other areas.
limitations: Area categories are not parcel-level hazard findings.

sources.name: Risk changes through building life
verified_claims: Building risks can change during occupation and refurbishment, requiring ongoing risk management.
limitations: A refurbishment does not automatically mean risk increased or decreased.

sources.name: Foreseeable scenario coverage
verified_claims: Building safety risk assessments should consider all foreseeable scenarios relevant to the building.
limitations: The published examples are not an exhaustive checklist for every building.

sources.name: Fire-spread scenarios
verified_claims: Fire scenarios can include single-floor, between-floor, multiple-floor and whole-building spread.
limitations: Scenario inclusion does not establish that fire spread has occurred.

sources.name: Evacuation and response scenarios
verified_claims: Assessments should consider failures of evacuation routes, early detection, access and other emergency-response factors.
limitations: A scenario is a planning assumption rather than an observed event.

sources.name: Safety-system failure scenario
verified_claims: Assessments should consider whether failure of one or more safety-system components could allow escalation.
limitations: Potential failure must not be represented as confirmed equipment failure.

sources.name: Structural scenario family
verified_claims: Structural scenarios can include local, multiple-floor or whole-building collapse, balconies, foundations, gas explosion and impact damage.
limitations: The scenario family is not evidence of a structural defect in a named building.

sources.name: Worst-case scenario inclusion
verified_claims: Scenario planning should include worst-case outcomes, including failed controls, incorrect assumptions and escalation.
limitations: Worst-case analysis must not be presented as the most likely outcome.

sources.name: Existing-control effectiveness
verified_claims: Accountable persons should check that controls for which they are responsible remain effective and operate as designed.
limitations: A documented control does not prove operational effectiveness without inspection or testing evidence.

sources.name: All-reasonable-steps context
verified_claims: What counts as reasonable depends on building-specific circumstances, existing controls, additional measures, added risks and proportionality of cost.
limitations: Cost or inconvenience alone must not be used as a universal reason to reject a safety measure.

sources.name: Risk-method fitness
verified_claims: The Act does not mandate one assessment method; the chosen method should be fit for purpose, proportionate to complexity and cover the full range of risks.
limitations: Use of a named methodology does not guarantee a complete or correct assessment.

sources.name: Risk-assessment records
verified_claims: Accountable persons should record assessments, track actions and recommendations to completion, maintain new information and explain rejected measures.
limitations: A recorded action is not evidence that it has been completed.
